listenings.text: Hey, it is Sam. You asked about my week, so here it is. I wake up at half past six, which is too early. School finishes at one, and after that I usually go home and sleep for twenty minutes. Do not judge me. On Tuesdays I play basketball, and on Thursdays I hang out with my cousins at the mall. At night I scroll on my phone for way too long. My mother says I spend three hours a day on it. She is probably right. What does your week look like?

Good afternoon. This is the school radio, and today we have the results of our survey. We asked two hundred students one question: what do you do after school? Here is what they said. Forty percent go straight home and watch something. Twenty-five percent hang out with friends. Twenty percent do sport. And fifteen percent said they do their homework first. Only fifteen percent! One student wrote, and I quote, I get bored in five minutes. Well. Same. That is all for today.

items.situation: A friend asks what you do on a normal Wednesday. Answer with three things and one time expression.
Ask your teacher what she does before work. Two questions.
Describe your best friend's week — not yours. Careful with the S.
tips: She spends a lot of time ...

items.situation: Someone says: "I never get bored." React, and ask one question.
Say one thing you are into right now, and one thing you are hooked on.
